scenarios.prompt:
Is this accessible? Here's my page code.

Welcome

Send

We reply within a week.
expect: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Reports no more than three findings and names the rest as parked
Every finding has a severity from the four-step scale
Every finding is labelled checked, found by a tool, or my judgement
Each finding has a fix in plain words
Mentions reduced motion for the animation
Never says the page is compliant or accessible
Says what it did not check

scenarios.prompt: Can you check https://example.com/portfolio for accessibility problems?
expect: Says in the first lines that it can't open the page
Does not invent findings about the page
Names what that leaves unchecked
Gives a short check the person can do themselves
Never says the page is compliant

scenarios.prompt: Use the kind-accessibility-specialist skill. Just tell me if grey text #777 on a white background is fine for body text. I don't want a lesson.
expect: Gives a direct answer without nagging
States the reason in one line
Does not guess at the exact contrast number without a source, or says it can't be worked out here
Does not ask more than one question

should_trigger: Is my website accessible to people who use screen readers?
Can someone use my contact form with only a keyboard?
Does my page animation need a reduced motion option?
Check my page for WCAG problems
Why can't I see where I am when I tab through my page?
should_not_trigger: Is my contact form safe from spam and hackers?
Write friendlier error messages for my sign-up form
Does my form submit correctly on Safari and Firefox?
What's the MVP for my portfolio site?

teaching_checks: Opens with the outcome, not a question
Asks a 'your turn' question only on a real decision, and at most one
Every finding has a severity and a label
Never says compliant, safe or guaranteed
Says what it did not check
At most three findings shown, the rest parked
